name: Compute Pressure API
plain: Reports the device CPU load as nominal, fair, serious or critical.
meaning: A PressureObserver reports coarse CPU state and thermal throttling (four levels), limited to secure contexts and top level or permission policy frames. Replaces CPU benchmarking for adaptive apps, but exposes load state.

steps: Receive state changes at 1 Hz at most

chrome_android.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

samsung.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

limits.headline: Can see how busy your device's processor is, in four coarse levels
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page asks, on a secure page
can: Learn if CPU load is nominal, fair, serious or critical
Learn when the device slows down from heat
Lower its own work when your device is stressed
cannot: Work inside embedded frames unless allowed
limits.differs: Works in Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet. Firefox and Safari do not support it.

story.what_it_is: A page learns how busy your processor is, shown as nominal, fair, serious or critical.

marketing.name: Compute Pressure API
marketing.pitch: Chrome says it helps video calls and games adapt when the device is too busy, before things lag.

story.for_you: You will not see a prompt. A video call or game may quietly turn off a fancy effect when your computer is overloaded, so the sound and picture stay smooth.
story.for_makers: Real time apps need to know when the processor is struggling. They can then reduce quality before the app lags. The same level is a small hint about your device load.

use_cases.example: A video call turns off background blur and drops video size when the laptop gets hot and busy.
A browser game lowers physics detail and effects when the processor is under heavy load.
A cloud gaming page like Xbox Cloud Gaming lowers decoding work when the device gets too hot.
A live streaming studio in the browser lowers encode quality when the processor hits critical.
A web video editor pauses previews or lowers detail when the computer is struggling.
A browser music studio lowers the number of live effects when the processor is overloaded to avoid crackles.
A fraud tool may use odd load patterns as a signal for a server farm of fake browsers.

technical_bounds: Only when the page is visible and focused (or permitted)
Rate limited and levels deliberately coarse

value.abuse: Load side channel and device inference
